title: Move-out cleaning checklist for Piedmont renters
description: A move out cleaning Piedmont SC checklist for renters: what landlords check, room-by-room tasks, and how a free in-home estimate sets your price.

takeaways: Walk through your lease and landlord checklist before you start cleaning.
Ovens, fridge interiors, baseboards and bathroom grout are the usual deposit problems.

html:
If your keys are due back on a Friday, the cleaning is not the part you want to be improvising on Thursday night. Renters in Piedmont, a mill town along the Saluda River where houses and apartments range from old mill-era homes to newer subdivisions off SC-20, tend to lose deposit money on a short list of the same spots. This checklist is in the order our team works through a house, so you can follow it yourself or use it to compare what a pro crew covers.

Before you clean: read the paperwork

Pull out your lease and any move-in condition report. Landlords usually compare the unit to that document, and normal wear is treated differently from dirt. Take dated photos of each room when you are done. If anything was already stained or damaged on day one, make sure your move-in notes say so.

The room-by-room checklist

Kitchen

  • Empty and wipe inside and outside of all cabinets and drawers.
  • Clean the oven, including racks, and the microwave inside and out.
  • Empty the refrigerator and freezer, wash shelves and bins, and leave doors propped open if it is unplugged.
  • Degrease the stovetop, range hood and backsplash.
  • Wipe the sink, faucet and the dishwasher front.

Bathrooms

  • Scrub the toilet including the base and behind it.
  • Clean shower walls, tub, glass tracks and grout lines.
  • Wipe vanity interiors, mirrors and light fixtures.

Bedrooms, closets and living areas

  • Clear closet shelves and rods, then wipe them and vacuum the floor.
  • Wipe baseboards, doors, door frames and light switches.
  • Clean window sills, tracks and blinds.
  • Vacuum carpet and mop hard floors edge to edge.

The spots that usually cost people their deposit

Based on the move-outs we see around the Upstate, the pattern repeats. The inside of the oven is first: baked-on grease does not wipe off in five minutes. The bottom of the refrigerator comes next, then the track of a sliding door, then the black line along bathroom grout. Baseboards and light switches round it out, because they are the places a landlord runs a finger. None of these are hard, just slow, and they are easy to run out of time for after carrying boxes all day.

Order matters

Clean from the top down and the back to the front. Dust the ceiling fans and vents before you vacuum, do the kitchen and bathrooms while you still have the water on, and finish with the floors as you walk out the door. If you mop first and then carry furniture across, you will do it twice. Our move-out cleaning in Piedmont crews work this same way, and the move-in and move-out cleaning page lists every task they cover.

What to expect if you hire it out

The estimate visit takes about as long as a walkthrough with the landlord would. Someone looks at each room, opens the oven and fridge, checks the bathrooms and asks about your key date. From there you get an exact price. On the day, the team arrives with their own supplies and equipment, works from the kitchen to the bathrooms to the bedrooms, and finishes with the floors so nobody walks over a wet mop path.

Renters in Piedmont often ask whether the cleaning will satisfy a landlord's inspection. We follow the same list landlords use, so the baseboards, grout, appliance interiors and window tracks all get attention, and the Brazilian detail-first method means we check edges and corners that a fast pass skips. We cannot control what a landlord decides, but a thorough clean with dated photos is the best evidence you can bring to a deposit conversation. If you used a cleaning service, keep the receipt too.

One last tip from the move-outs we see: leave the lights on, open the blinds and walk the unit at midday. Smudges on mirrors and handprints on doors show up under daylight in a way they never do at night.

How much does move-out cleaning cost in Piedmont?

There is no honest flat number, because a one-bedroom left tidy and a four-bedroom with a greasy oven are different jobs. The price depends on home size (rooms and square feet), the condition the last occupant left it in, whether the oven and refrigerator need heavy work, whether the home is empty or still furnished (empty homes clean faster), and how tight your timing is. A closing-day deadline can mean a larger team.

How long it takes, and booking this week

Doing it yourself, a typical apartment can eat a full day of evenings. A professional team is faster because there are several people working different rooms at once, but we still plan around the home. If your move date is close, book the estimate now and tell us the deadline. We are 21 miles and about 35 minutes from Greer, so scheduling around a Piedmont key-return date is something we can do.

DIY or hire it out?

Do it yourself if the unit is small and in decent shape. Hire it out if you are managing a work shift, kids or a long drive between the old place and the new one. People moving between Piedmont and nearby towns such as Pelzer often find the cleaning is the one task they can hand off.
